thread:
customer_acme_ops: Hey team — hitting intermittent 400s from /v1/embeddings when using the TypeScript SDK. Error payload includes "dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 768". This only happens when we send batched requests from our worker pool (concurrency=4). Single requests are fine. Happening under bursty load. Any pointers?

maria_support: Sorry about that — can you share the TS SDK version, a minimal repro snippet, and one example request_id or trace id from a failed call? Also, are you batching on the client or server side?

customer_acme_ops: TS SDK v1.4.2. We're batching on the client (we split inputs into chunks of up to 8 and call embeddings.create on each chunk concurrently). Example snippet:

```
const batches = chunkArray(inputs, 8);
await Promise.all(batches.map(b => client.embeddings.create({ model: 'rwd-embed-large', input: b })));
```

Failed request id from headers: rwd-req-5839a2

sam_ts_sdk: Thanks. That pattern rings a bell. Two quick asks: (1) try running with concurrency=1 and confirm if errors stop, (2) capture the request body we send to the API for a failing batch (should be an array of strings). Can you attach a sample failed payload?

customer_acme_ops: Ran with concurrency=1 — errors stopped. Here's an anonymized failing payload we captured (one of the concurrent batches):

```
{ model: 'rwd-embed-large', input: ['short text', 'some longer text', ...] }
```

But the 400 response body included: "expected 1536 got 768" which suggests half-size vectors for some items in that batch.

leo_ml: Short hypothesis: sounds like a bug in the TS SDK client-side batching implementation when multiple concurrent batches are in-flight. Possibly buffers are being reused or inputs are being flattened incorrectly under concurrency, producing mis-sized requests to the server (or the server receives mismatched input lengths). The fact concurrency=1 fixes it supports that.

maria_support: For immediate mitigation: (1) set client concurrency to 1 or (2) set batch size to 1 (disable batching) and (3) temporarily disable client retries so partial retries don't re-send wrong payloads. Example config tweaks:

```
// reduce concurrency
await workerPool.process({ concurrency: 1 });

// or disable client batch/atomic grouping (pseudo-config)
client = new RedwoodClient({ batching: { enabled: false } });

// disable retries
client.config({ retryOptions: { retries: 0 } });
```

sam_ts_sdk: Internal note: we reproduced locally with a stress script. Minimal repro command (run from package root):

```
node ./scripts/repro/ts-embed-concurrency-repro.js --concurrency 5 --batchSize 8
```

Repro gist: the SDK's batch serializer reuses an internal buffer when multiple Promise chains interleave; under heavy concurrency a slice offset bug causes half-length payloads to be sent for some entries. We've isolated the bug to buffer slice math in src/batching/serializer.ts line ~87.

ci-bot: Deploy check started for branch fix/ts-batch-serializer -> CI pipeline queued

sam_ts_sdk: Patch is merged to main and queued for a 1.4.3 patch release. ETA ~2 hours for canary npm release. Workarounds until then: pin to 1.4.1 or use the concurrency=1 setting. Also disabling client-side batching avoids the code path.

customer_acme_ops: Great — can you share the temporary repro script or the exact command you ran so we can validate once the patch is out?

sam_ts_sdk: Pushed a small repro into the repo under scripts/repro (we referenced it above). Snippet of what it does:

```
// pseudo
for (let i=0;i<1000;i++) {
  createRandomStrings(8)
  .then(batch => client.embeddings.create({ model:'rwd-embed-large', input:batch }))
}

Run with node scripts/repro/ts-embed-concurrency-repro.js --concurrency 5
```

maria_support: Once you are able to test canary, please report back with the same request_id header (rwd-req-5839a2 or new ones) so we can validate server logs. We'll also correlate with internal request logs.

customer_acme_ops: Will try the canary once available. For immediate safety we set concurrency to 1 and disabled retries. No 400s in the last 30 minutes. Thanks for quick turnaround.

sam_ts_sdk: Apologies for the disruption — we'll post release notes when 1.4.3 is published and follow up in this thread. If you need an urgent backport build, DM me and I can share a tarball.

leo_ml: Follow-on: we'll add a small fuzz test around concurrency/batching to our CI to prevent regression (tracking issue INF-784).

customer_acme_ops: Thanks all. Leaving this open to verify post-canary, will update when we validate.

maria_support: Noted — keeping thread open. :thumbsup:
